columns.name: Penalty or reward function form
columns.rationale: The question asks whether the optimal-versus-heuristic gap depends on the age or fidelity penalty function, so the function used must be recorded per source.

columns.instruction: Report any structural property the source states for its optimal policy (for example threshold structure, state-dependent threshold, monotonicity), in the source's wording. Take the property stated for the main model. The column does not apply if the source derives no optimal policy.
columns.name: Structure of the optimal policy
columns.rationale: A stated threshold or index-like structure of the optimal policy indicates when a simple heuristic can match it, which bears on the size of the performance gap.

columns.instruction: Report what the source states about how the advantage of the optimal or proposed policy over heuristics or baselines changes with system parameters such as generation probability, memory size, decoherence, number of hops or users, or target fidelity. Use the source's wording and numbers. The column does not apply if no such dependence is stated.
columns.name: Gap dependence on system parameters
columns.rationale: Regime-dependence of the gap on parameters other than the penalty function helps interpret whether gaps reported across sources are comparable.

columns.instruction: Report what the source states about how the relative performance of policies changes with delayed or missing knowledge of link/channel state, or with memoryless versus time-correlated (Markov) channels. Use the source's wording. The column does not apply if the source considers only one channel-information and channel-dynamics assumption and does not vary it.
columns.name: Gap dependence on channel information or channel dynamics
columns.rationale: The question asks specifically whether the gap depends on delayed channel state information or a time-varying Markov channel, which the current choice columns record only as assumptions, not as a varied effect.

columns.instruction: How does the source model loss of stored entanglement over time? Choose the model the main results rest on.
columns.name: Entanglement decoherence model
columns.rationale: Age and fidelity penalties only matter when stored entanglement degrades, so the decoherence model determines whether a penalty-function dependence can arise.

columns.instruction: Does the source state that computing its optimal policy is limited by state-space size or computational cost, motivating heuristic, index or learned approximations? Answer yes only if the source states such a limitation; answer no if it states the optimal policy is tractable for its settings.
columns.name: Scalability of the optimal policy
columns.rationale: The trade-off between optimality and computational cost explains why heuristic or index policies are compared against MDP/LP benchmarks at all.

columns.instruction: How does the source obtain the performance of the compared policies? Choose every method the source states.
columns.name: Evaluation method
columns.rationale: Whether a reported gap is proven, computed or simulated affects how gaps from different sources can be compared.

Two rows share the title 'Optimal Scheduling in a Quantum Switch: Capacity and Throughput Optimality' with identical abstracts and are likely versions of one work, not independent evidence.
